The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress for the 2027 election, Peter Obi, has endorsed SmartBallot, a technology platform designed to support grassroots mobilisation, civic engagement and election monitoring. Obi urged supporters and candidates of the party to register on the platform and explore its tools for organising communities, coordinating voters and polling unit agents, and monitoring elections. The former Anambra State governor made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Sunday. “I am pleased to endorse SmartBallot (http://smartballotapp.com), a platform developed to facilitate grassroots mobilisation, civic engagement, and election monitoring. “I urge our supporters and NDC candidates to register on SmartBallot and examine how its tools can assist them in organizing their communities, coordinating voters and polling unit agents, expanding grassroots engagement, and supporting transparent election monitoring,” he wrote. It enables communication, voter coordination and observation activities. On election day, agents can upload result sheets from polling units, allowing users to track reported figures alongside official processes. The platform stresses that it is not an official electoral body and does not replace the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Its public-election features are limited to lawful civic engagement, voter education, voluntary mobilisation, community organisation and election observation. Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the Labour Party platform, is the NDC’s standard-bearer for the 2027 general elections. The endorsement comes as political parties and civic groups intensify preparations for the polls, with renewed focus on technology-driven tools to improve transparency and participation.
